title.en: Early humans and the start of farming

text.en:
Long, long ago a group of people travelled from place to place hunting animals and collecting fruits. One day they dropped some seeds near a stream.
When they returned, green plants had grown.
"We can grow our own food!" said an old woman.

Early humans lived by hunting animals and gathering fruits, roots and seeds. They moved from place to place looking for food and lived in caves or rough shelters. They made tools from stone and learned to use fire.
About ten thousand years ago people began to grow crops and tame animals such as cattle and goats. This is called farming and herding.
Farming made people settle in one place, build houses, store grains and later form villages and towns. In India early farming villages grew in places such as Mehrgarh.
Early humans hunted animals and gathered fruits. They moved to find food.
They made stone tools and learned to use fire.
Later people began to grow crops and tame animals. This is farming.
Farming made people settle, build houses and store grain.

problem.en: How did farming change the way people lived?

text.en: Before farming people moved around to find food.
With farming they could grow food in one place.
So they built houses and villages and stored grain.

prompt.en: A friend says early humans lived in houses like ours. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Early humans lived in caves or rough shelters.
Houses came after farming made people settle.

points.en: Early humans hunted and gathered food.
Farming began about ten thousand years ago.
Farming led to settled life and villages.
